What languages should be known to start to learn hacking?
English helps a lot. So you're already well on your way there.
Depends on what you want to hack into. Probably php/javascript a good starting place.
I actually have no idea, but is knowing C++ and Python any help for hacking?

It doesn't hurt and it might help... It's just like others have said though, it all depends what you want to do. If you plan to exploit programs and the likes, then it'll probably help having that understanding. If you're exploiting websites you might want to know more web-based languages but C++ and python could still probably be used to make tools to exploit whatever you need... but you still need to have an understanding of what you're exploiting, or at least that's what I believe.

C, Python, PHP, Perl, Ruby, Bash (or other shell), are the most common when it comes to exploit code in the wild. That is; If you want to understand what other peoples scripts are doing from places such as https://www.exploit-db.com/ to learn how the exploit process happens. Those would be the languages to get familiar with. C is more often used for local exploits.

Javascript may be a bonus too. If you're interested in browser based attacks.

Most of the time, you'll be told PHP/JavaScript. While these are useful languages to know for looking through code and such, chances are you wont be programming in them very often while hacking.

It mostly boils down to what you want to hack. For websites or web-based things, I usually use Java, but other languages that have simple to use HTTP Wrappers such as Python also work. I'm not saying you can't use C/C++ for those kinds of things, its just much harder.

If you're looking to do things like finding vulnerabilities in operating systems and reverse engineering programs and stuff, you're going to be looking at 80x86/64-bit assembly, along with C and/or C++, without a doubt.

Hope this helps! :) If you have any other questions or need any other help, feel free to comment or PM me.

Why use Java for web-based targets?

I use Java for web-based targets because it has really easy-to-use HTTP wrappers, which make it fun and easy to manipulate HTTP requests for bots and things like that.

I think anyone getting into hacking should at least be able to READ C/C++/ObjC, but should be proficient in a scripting language as well as a portable compiled language (e.g. C, Java, C#, etc.) and x86_64 assembler (at least to some level.) It would also be eminently useful to know SQL.

That's my take on it.

It depends on what your aims are. If you are looking at web-server exploitation, Javascript/PHP and a function knowledge of SQL databases are always a bonus. For server exploits, you are mostly looking at C/C++, ASM is handy, and python is always handy to automate your attacks. If you are looking at embedded devices i.e phones/tablets/routers then you're going to want to take a look at MIPS, C++ and Python again. Those list about three potential targets out of a possible 500. Hacking isn't strictly limited to a blanket "I know how to program XXXXX" I can hack anything!
